bibliography.record: S4, S7, S8 and S9 come from the same group (GeWu-Lab, Di Hu, Renmin University) and share datasets (CREMA-D, Kinetics-Sounds) and code base; S1, S2 and S6 share authors (Hang Zhao, Yu Huang, Chenzhuang Du, Longbo Huang). full_text_checked: Read via HTML (ar5iv / arxiv.org/html, through a summarising fetch tool, so numbers were extracted by that tool and cross-checked only for internal consistency): S6 main text and appendix up to character 100000 of 115848 (Tables 1-10, 12-14, 18-19, 22; final ~16k characters not read); S4 main text (Tables 1-6, method equations); S3 main text (Definitions 4.1, 5.1, Algorithm 1, results table); S1 main text (Theorems 1-2, Tables 1-3, 5); S2 first 100000 of 185103 characters (data model, Theorems 5.1-5.2, Corollary 5.3, Figure 1 description; later appendix proofs not read); S5 main text (Tables 1-4, 6); S7 main text (Tables 1-4; supplementary ablations NOT accessible); S8 main text (Tables 1-5, 7; gradient statistics only in figures); S9 main results section (Table 2 summary). PMLR page of S2 seen through search snippet only. No code repository was opened. Local project files opened: runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json (paired utility, identity AUC, counts), runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_D.npz (array shapes only: F1 8326x18x238, Gtag 8326x18x10, ident 8326x18, uid 8326), protocol.json (split names fit84/fit20/evaluate26). No figures were viewed directly; any curve-only results (OGM-GE Fig. 1, PMR Fig. 4, D&R Fig. 1, MMPareto Fig. 1/4/5) are reported only as the authors' textual claims.
inputs_state_output: Authors' setting (all sources): two or three modalities (audio vs video frames on CREMA-D/Kinetics-Sounds/VGGSound/AVE; RGB vs optical flow on UCF101; front vs rear view on ModelNet40; RGB vs depth on NVGesture; colour vs grey MNIST), each with its OWN trainable encoder (ResNet-18, I3D, SlowFast, small CNN, MBT transformer), fused late (concat, sum, FiLM, gated, linear/MLP/attention head) or intermediately (MMTM in S3), output = one class label per clip; no temporal tracking state beyond what the video encoder pools. The 'strong' modality is defined empirically as the one learned faster / with higher correct-class confidence (audio on CREMA-D and Kinetics-Sounds; depth on NVGesture; RGB on UCF101), the 'weak' one is still substantially informative alone (e.g. CREMA-D visual-only 41.9 vs audio-only 52.5 in S4 Table 1; UCF101 flow-only 74.99 vs RGB 77.08 in S6 Table 1). Ours: strong base = FROZEN pre-trained MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance of each real detection region, reduced to cosines to snapped exemplar / previous target / bank plus 32 PCA products; added branch = SAVED FlyVis activity (68 regional features: 34 output types incl. T4/T5 + 6-neighbour means) from a bounded grey crop around the tracker prediction, with recurrent state run over exemplar+search frames, plus geometry and assignment context; per episode up to 18 candidate regions (train26 arrays: 8326 episodes x 18 candidates x 238 features); output = per-candidate identity probability, then a separate gate that transfers the full box. Crucial differences: (1) in our pipeline NEITHER branch's representation is trained during fusion (MASA frozen, FlyVis activity saved), so the encoder-level competition of S2/S6 (encoder of the losing modality never learns its features) cannot occur in the experiments already run; only head-level reliance (S6 Table 4 'laziness' of a jointly trained head on frozen unimodal encoders) can; (2) the task is ranking one target among neighbours inside an episode, not clip classification; (3) our 'weak' branch is not weak in row-level separability (FlyVis alone AUC 0.950-0.956 vs appearance 0.965, report.json -> identity), but a large part of that separability is shared with no-fly geometry (0.92-0.93). The imbalance literature becomes directly relevant only for the untried option of fine-tuning the FlyVis core jointly with an identity loss next to appearance.
fusion_and_training: S4 OGM-GE: per mini-batch, s_i^u = softmax probability of the correct class from modality u's partial logit (fusion weights split, bias b/2); discrepancy ratio rho^u = sum_i s_i^u / sum_i s_i^other; dominant modality's encoder gradient multiplied by k^u = 1 - tanh(alpha*rho^u) when rho^u > 1 (else 1); GE adds Gaussian noise with SGD covariance to restore generalisation; alpha chosen in [0,1] on validation; both encoders trained from scratch. S5 PMR: per-modality class prototypes (momentum-updated on 1/10 of training data) act as non-parametric classifiers; prototypical cross-entropy pushes the slower modality toward its prototypes, weighted by the prototype-based imbalance ratio; prototypical entropy regularisation slows the dominant modality only in the first epochs. S3 Greedy: intermediate MMTM fusion; conditional learning speed from cumulative ||G||^2/||theta||^2 of fusion vs branch parameters; when |d_speed| > alpha, Q re-balancing steps accelerate the slower branch with the other branch's features replaced by training means; 'random' variant samples step types uniformly. S6 UMT: unimodal encoders first trained alone (frozen teachers); the late-fusion model is trained from scratch with CE on the fused output + MSE feature distillation of each encoder's pre-fusion feature toward its teacher (weight 50; S6 Table 13 sweep 0..100); UME: train each unimodal model alone and average predictions, no joint training at all. S7 D&R: every H epochs each encoder is softly re-initialised theta = (1-a)theta + a*theta_init with a = tanh(lambda*g), g = |purity_train - purity_val| of k-means clustering of that encoder's features; well-learnt (over-fitting) modalities are reset more, weak ones less. S8 MMPareto: joint loss + one unimodal CE loss per modality on each encoder; when unimodal and multimodal gradients conflict (negative cosine) use the Pareto direction rescaled to the magnitude of the uniform sum (gamma = 1.5), else plain sum. None of these sources uses zero-init residual alpha over a frozen base (that is C01); the closest analogues to 'protect the base, do not ignore the added branch' are UME (base untouched, branch trained alone, late averaging), UMT (branch distilled from its own unimodal teacher) and MMPareto (auxiliary unimodal loss on the weak branch). In our current pipeline fusion = concatenation of fixed feature blocks into one gradient-boosting model with nested folds; nothing is frozen/unfrozen and no branch-level loss exists.
labels_and_loss: All sources: clip-level class labels (6 emotions on CREMA-D, 31-32 classes Kinetics-Sounds, 309 VGGSound, 101 UCF101, 40 ModelNet40, 25 NVGesture), softmax cross-entropy on the fused output; S6 adds feature MSE to unimodal teachers; S8 adds per-modality CE heads; S5 adds prototypical CE and entropy terms; S3 adds no loss, changes the update schedule. No pairs/triplets, no contrastive identity loss, no explicit hard-negative mining, no treatment of 'similar neighbours'. Class balance is not the issue studied; 'imbalance' means modality reliance, not label frequency. Ours: binary per-candidate label 'this region is our target' (train26: 5345 labelled rows, 928 positives, report.json -> identity), log-loss of gradient boosting; hard negatives are the other detections in the same episode (neighbours), implicitly present because each episode contains up to 18 candidates; downstream consequence measured as offline utility (helpful-harmful)/known. Transfer note: the imbalance diagnostics (S3 utilization, S4 ratio, S5 prototype confidence) must be computed per episode on the candidate-ranking task (correct-candidate softmax over the 18 regions), not on row-level binary AUC, otherwise easy far-away negatives dominate and mask whether the fly branch helps on neighbour confusions.
data_camera_resolution_rate: S4/S5/S7/S8/S9: CREMA-D (acted audio-visual emotion clips, ~7.4k clips, static camera, frontal faces, studio lighting), Kinetics-Sounds and VGGSound (YouTube clips, varied cameras), AVE (audio-visual event localisation), UCF101 RGB + optical flow (YouTube action clips, 320x240 source, moving camera), CMU-MOSI/MOSEI (text/audio/video sentiment), Food-101, BalancedAV; S3: Colored-and-gray MNIST, ModelNet40 two rendered views, NVGesture RGB/depth; S1: IEMOCAP; S2: synthetic sparse-coding data and an item-classification image+text set. Frames are typically sampled sparsely (one or a few frames per clip for the visual branch, e.g. 1-3 frames at 224x224 in the OGM-GE code lineage) [uncertain: exact sampling not verified in the papers read]. None of the datasets involves multi-object tracking, identity among similar neighbours, night driving, glare or BDD100K. Ours: BDD100K MOT train130 (fit104/train26 splits; train26 used only once for the pre-registered hybrid check), dash camera moving, 30 fps source, low light/glare/occlusion/clutter, FlyVis sees a bounded grey crop on 721 hexagonal columns.

S5 Table 2 CREMA-D concat 53.2 -> PMR 61.1 (OGM-GE 57.7 in their re-run). S7 Table 1 CREMA-D joint 67.47 -> D&R 75.13; Kinetics-Sounds 65.04 -> 69.10; UCF101 80.41 -> 82.11; S7 Table 4 with a scarcely informative (noisy) audio: joint 65.86, OGM-GE 62.63, G-Blending 61.16, AGM 62.87 (all WORSE than joint), D&R 69.49. (4) Independent-toolkit re-run S9 Table 2 (accuracy): best method per dataset differs (MMPareto on KS 74.55 vs baseline 65.63, CREMA-D 79.97 vs 65.50, CMU-MOSEI 81.18 vs 78.99; AMCo UCF101 86.91 vs 81.80; MLA Food-101 93.14 vs 91.65; AGM BalancedAV 75.49 vs 73.33; UMT VGGSound 51.58 vs 48.08); 6 of 116 method-dataset results fall below baseline; on CMU-MOSEI text-only 80.58 beats the multimodal baseline 78.99. (5) Diagnostic numbers: S3 NVGesture u(depth|RGB) = 0.63 vs u(RGB|depth) = 0.01; E[d_util] ModelNet40 about -0.1 vanilla -> about 0.0 guided. Ours (for contrast, from runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json): identity AUC appearance 0.9646, +D 0.9728, +C 0.9714, +R1 0.9708 (n 5345, 928 positives); utility per video: appearance-baseline +0.660 [+0.035; +1.302] pp, (appearance+D)-appearance +0.106 [-0.176; +0.400], (appearance+D)-(appearance+R1) -0.042 [-0.358; +0.280], (appearance+D)-(appearance+C) -0.095 [-0.403; +0.228], true identity-baseline +2.836 [+1.873; +3.831].
distinguishing_ablations: Ablations that separate 'imbalance' from 'no extra information': (a) S6 Table 3 is the key one - it compares, with FROZEN unimodally trained encoders, a jointly trained multimodal linear classifier against simple averaging of the unimodal predictions; where averaging wins (UCF101, ModelNet40) the joint head under-uses one modality (head-level laziness, S6 Table 4), where the joint head wins (VGG-Sound, Kinetics-400) cross-modal interaction carries real extra information. (b) S6 Tables 1 and 7, S8 Table 1: linear probes of each encoder after joint training vs after unimodal training - imbalance shows as a large probe drop for the weak modality (UCF101 flow 74.99 -> 48.08; CREMA-D video 56.05 -> 36.56); redundancy would show no drop. (c) S3: identical-input control (both branches given the same modality) gives E[d_util] near 0, showing the utilization measure detects reliance, not information content. (d) S6 Table 8: self-distillation without a unimodal teacher (49.7-49.9) vs UMT 53.5 on VGG-Sound - the gain comes from unimodal pre-training, not from distillation regularisation itself; S6 Table 14: modality-wise dropout 51.37 recovers part of the gap, UMT 53.46. (e) S8 Table 1: 'unimodal pre-trained & fine-tune' (71.51 CREMA-D, 68.75 KS) already equals the uniform multitask baseline (71.10, 68.31) and beats OGM-GE/PMR/Greedy/AGM re-runs, i.e. once encoders are pre-trained alone, gradient-modulation gains largely vanish and only MMPareto adds ~+3.6 / +1.4 pp. (f) Negative results: S7 Table 4 - when the added modality is scarcely informative (noisy audio), gradient-modulation methods HURT (OGM-GE 62.63, G-Blending 61.16 vs joint 65.86); S3 NVGesture-pretrained guided 83.82 +/- 1.45 vs vanilla 83.20 +/- 0.21 (no clear gain); S9: no method consistently best, six results below baseline, CMU-MOSEI unimodal text beats multimodal baseline. Missing in all sources: an equal-capacity NON-informative branch control (e.g. shuffled or random second modality of the same size) - so 'gain from a weak branch' is never separated from 'gain from extra capacity/regularisation'; seeds: S3 reports mean +/- std over runs, S6 ModelNet40 Table 10 too; S4, S5, S7, S8 tables are single numbers without variance [uncertain whether multiple seeds were averaged].
explanations_addressed: E1 'fly carries no unique identity information beyond appearance' - DESIGN ANALOGY / CAUTION: S1-S2 assume each modality carries label signal; S7 Table 4 shows that boosting a scarcely informative branch harms; S6 Table 3 gives the operational test (late average vs joint head on frozen unimodal models). Our data already lean toward E1-like redundancy at the level of the fly TRANSFORM: (appearance+D) is not better than (appearance+R1) (-0.042 [-0.358; +0.280]) or stock C, and their AUC gains over appearance are nearly identical (0.0082 vs 0.0062 vs 0.0068), i.e. whatever extra signal enters is equally present in the raw eye input. Imbalance remedies amplify a weak branch; they cannot create FlyVis-specific information that R1 lacks. E2 'information exists but fusion/training ignores it (modality imbalance)' - DIRECT THEORY + DIAGNOSTIC: S2 and S6 show this happens mainly when encoders are trained jointly from scratch; with frozen pre-trained features only head-level laziness remains (S6 Table 4). Gradient boosting on concatenated fixed features is a greedy learner too (early trees pick the strongest appearance cosines), but it keeps fitting residuals, so starvation should be weaker than in a neural head; this is testable cheaply (see math_precheck: late fusion of separately trained appearance-only and fly-only models, and residual boosting from the appearance offset). Evidence against E2 in our numbers: fly features ARE used jointly (AUC +0.008), the gain just does not reach utility and does not beat R1. E3 'saved readout features lost it, new activity or fine-tuned core needed' - DESIGN ANALOGY: S6/S8 show that a branch's own representation must be learned with its own (unimodal) objective; for FlyVis this means any core fine-tuning on identity should be done unimodally first (UMT/UME logic) or with an auxiliary fly-only identity loss (MMPareto), NOT only through the joint loss next to frozen MASA, where the residual gradient is small (appearance already fits ~96% AUC) and the fly branch would be starved (S2 mechanism). E4 'FlyVis lacks a lobula/object pathway' - NOT ADDRESSED. E5 'motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging' - PARTIAL/CAUTION: S9 shows gains are dataset-dependent and S7 shows harm where a modality is uninformative; no source stratifies by condition; the transfer implies computing utilization/complementarity per regime (darkness, glare, occlusion, same-class neighbours). E6 'ceiling too low' - NOT ADDRESSED by the sources, but the typical remedy gains (+1.5 to +10 accuracy points in classification, S4-S8) come from settings where the weak modality alone reaches 40-75% of a multi-class task and is learned from scratch; our headroom is the gap between appearance +0.66 pp and perfect identity +2.84 pp, i.e. about 2.2 pp of utility, of which a fly branch would need to capture a large share to matter.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (ICML/CVPR/NeurIPS/ECCV) for S1-S8 (S2 venue confirmed via PMLR; others from repo names/keywords and general knowledge, marked uncertain), BalanceBenchmark S9 a preprint. Code links exist for S3, S4, S7, S8 (not opened, so not verified to run). Replication: the phenomenon (weak-modality encoder starvation, joint <= best unimodal in some setups) is reproduced across groups and datasets (S3, S4, S5, S6, S8, S9) - STRONG for the existence of imbalance in jointly trained neural encoders on audio-visual/RGB-flow classification. The size and ranking of remedies is MODERATE-to-WEAK: tables are mostly single runs, re-runs of OGM-GE/PMR differ strongly across papers (CREMA-D OGM-GE 61.9 in S4, 57.7 in S5, 68.95 in S7, 69.19 in S8 with different baselines), no method is consistently best (S9), and none includes an equal-capacity non-informative branch control. Relevance to our frozen-feature, ranking-among-neighbours setting: WEAK as direct evidence, MODERATE as a source of diagnostics and of the UME/UMT decision rule.
difference_from_tried: What we tried is late-ish feature-level fusion: fixed MASA cosines/PCA products + fixed FlyVis D/C/R1 activity concatenated into one gradient-boosting identity model (nested folds), neighbour-relative features, tagged previous target, bank, T4/T5 motion consistency. Not yet tried and implied by these sources: (1) UME-style decision-level fusion - separate appearance-only and fly-only identity models, each tuned alone, combined by summed logits or a 2-input stacker, compared to the joint concatenated model (S6 Table 3 rule); (2) residual/offset boosting - fly-only trees fitted on top of the appearance model's out-of-fold logit (forces the branch to model only what appearance misses; a boosting analogue of protecting the base); (3) per-episode diagnostics of reliance (S3 conditional utilization: accuracy drop when fly features are replaced by their training mean or permuted within episode) and of per-branch confidence ratio on the correct candidate (S4 rho, S5 prototype ratio); (4) for the prepared core fine-tuning: train the FlyVis core on identity ALONE first (UMT teacher / UME member) or with an auxiliary fly-only identity loss (MMPareto), instead of only through a joint loss next to frozen MASA. Gradient modulation itself (OGM-GE, PMR, Greedy, D&R) has no counterpart in our current pipeline because no appearance encoder is trained; it becomes applicable only if MASA were unfrozen, which is outside the FlyVis-only scope rule.
math_precheck: All on CPU with already saved arrays (e.g. runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/train26_features_{D,C,R1}.npz: F1 8326x18x238, ident 8326x18; the same for fit104 via nested folds), no core training. Work at EPISODE level: target = which of up to 18 candidates is the tracked object. Step 0 (unimodal models, nested folds by video): out-of-fold candidate scores s_A (appearance only), s_F (FlyVis D only, without geometry), s_C, s_R1 (eye input only), s_G (geometry only), s_Fsh (FlyVis D with features permuted across candidates within an episode = equal-dimension non-informative control). Step 1 - S6 selection rule (imbalance vs redundancy at the head): compare per-episode top-1 identity and log-loss of (i) joint boosting [A,F] (already have), (ii) UME = s_A + s_F logits, (iii) 2-input logistic stacker on (s_A, s_F); repeat with R1 in place of F. Imbalance signature: (ii) or (iii) beats (i) with paired bootstrap CI over videos above 0. Redundancy signature: (i) ~ (ii) ~ (iii) ~ A alone. Step 2 - conditional usable information (link to C03): residual boosting with init_score = OOF logit of s_A, fitted on F only; Delta_F = log-loss(A) - log-loss(A + residual F) on held-out folds, same for R1, C, G and F-shuffled; report Delta_F - Delta_R1 and Delta_F - Delta_Fsh with video bootstrap CIs. Step 3 - S3 conditional utilization of the existing joint model: u(F|A) = (Acc_top1(A,F) - Acc_top1(A, F replaced by its training mean or within-episode permutation)) / Acc_top1(A,F). If Step 2 shows Delta_F > 0 but u(F|A) ~ 0 the joint model ignores available fly information (imbalance) -> late fusion/residual is the remedy; if both ~ 0 -> redundancy. Step 4 - error complementarity: 2x2 table of top-1 correctness of A vs F per episode; n10 = F right & A wrong, n01 = A right & F wrong; Yule's Q of errors; the same table for A vs R1 and A vs G. FlyVis-specific complementarity = n10(F) - n10(R1) (McNemar-style, bootstrap over videos). Step 5 - stratification (E5): repeat Steps 2 and 4 in strata - A-ambiguous episodes (top-2 appearance margin below its 20th percentile, or A wrong), same-class neighbour within k box widths, night/low luminance, glare, occlusion/re-appearance; report per stratum with CIs and counts (small strata -> descriptive only). Step 6 - translation into the bench's own currency (no foreign numbers): build an OR-oracle identity = true identity on episodes where A or F is top-1 correct, A's choice otherwise; pass it through the existing offline gate/utility code without retraining (threshold re-chosen on calibration videos exactly as before) to get U_OR(A,F); do the same for U_OR(A,R1) and U_OR(A,Fsh). This is an UPPER bound for ANY fusion/training of these two branches (including joint training with perfect balancing) given the current features. Known anchors: U(A) - baseline +0.660 pp, U(true identity) - baseline +2.836 pp (report.json). Decision rule (to be pre-registered by the author before computing): STOP GPU core fine-tuning on this route if any of: (a) upper 95% CI of [U_OR(A,F) - U_OR(A,R1)] <= 0 (no FlyVis-specific complementarity even for an oracle combiner); (b) upper CI of [U_OR(A,F) - U(A)] is below the minimal useful fly increment (proposal: +0.5 pp; the overall +2 pp criterion is unreachable if U_OR(A,F) - baseline < +2 pp) [uncertain: threshold is a proposal, not a project rule]; (c) Delta_F - Delta_R1 CI includes 0 in every stratum with >= 100 episodes. PROCEED to a CPU late-fusion/residual readout (not GPU) if Step 1 shows the imbalance signature; PROCEED to GPU core fine-tuning only if (a) and (b) pass AND the oracle gap is concentrated in a stratum where R1/geometry are also wrong (i.e. a motion-specific regime), because only then can a better-trained fly representation plausibly capture it. Caveat: the OR-oracle uses labels and is optimistic; with the unimodal fly model at 0.95 AUC some n10 episodes will be chance agreements - hence the obligatory F-shuffled and R1 oracles as nulls.
cue_role_and_regime: In the sources the weak modality enters as a parallel classification branch (feature fused late or intermediately), and the remedies act as training-time regularisers/schedulers (gradient scaling, prototype losses, re-initialisation, auxiliary unimodal losses, distillation targets); at inference nothing changes except the learned weights (UME: decision-level averaging). No source targets neighbour ambiguity, crossing paths, occlusion or darkness; the regime is 'whole-clip class decided by two sensory streams'. For us the transferable roles are: (1) decision-level fusion of a separately trained fly identity score with the appearance score (UME), (2) training-only regulariser for a future fly-core fine-tuning (auxiliary fly-only identity loss, UMT-style distillation target), (3) diagnostic of reliance per regime. The regime where a motion branch could plausibly be non-redundant with MASA is same-class, similar-look neighbours with different motion (crossing or adjacent vehicles), dark/glare frames where RoIAlign appearance degrades, and short occlusions; this must be verified by the stratified Steps 4-5 of math_precheck, since nothing in the imbalance literature says where a weak branch helps in tracking.
no_fly_equivalent_control: For each fusion variant derived from these sources, the same variant with the fly block replaced by: (1) eye input R1 (same crop, no FlyVis transform) - the decisive control because it already matches D (report.json: -0.042 [-0.358; +0.280]); (2) stock FlyVis C (modernisation control); (3) geometry/velocity-direction/Kalman-residual features of equal count (no-fly motion cue); (4) within-episode permuted fly features of equal dimension (non-informative equal-capacity branch - missing in all imbalance papers, required here); (5) for a future trained branch, an unconstrained small MLP/GRU of equal parameter count (~734) trained with the same unimodal-then-fuse schedule on R1 crops. A FlyVis result requires (A + fly via scheme X) > (A + R1 via scheme X) and > (A + permuted fly via X) with paired video bootstrap CIs.
bio_node_mapping: Not a biological mechanism; it is a training/fusion methodology. Mapped FlyVis nodes: readout (decision-level fusion, residual boosting over the appearance offset, per-branch identity head) and, for the untried core fine-tuning, the training objective of the connectome-constrained parameters (734 parameters; FlyWire-783-derived connectivity stays fixed, only the trained parameters move). A UMT-style fly-only identity pre-training would act on T4/T5 and other output types through their dynamics parameters; no lobula/LC node is implied.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior claims: UMT/UME (S6) and MMPareto (S8) already state that a weak branch should be trained with its own unimodal objective and fused late; our version would only differ in applying the selection rule to a frozen connectome-constrained motion model versus frozen appearance in MOT identity - a methodological use, not a novelty point.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis readout (CPU) first, core objective (GPU) only conditionally. Change R-UME: replace concatenation-into-one-booster by two separately trained identity heads (appearance-only head = part of the environment; fly-only head on FlyVis activity = our readout node) combined by summed logits or a 2-parameter stacker fitted on calibration videos; variant R-RES: fly head boosted on top of the appearance out-of-fold logit (residual, base untouched). Why it addresses a FlyVis problem: it isolates and protects the fly readout from being swamped by the stronger appearance cosines (S2/S6 head-level laziness) and makes the fly contribution measurable as its own term. Equal controls (same scheme, same capacity, same folds): appearance only; appearance + stock C; appearance + eye input R1; appearance + within-episode permuted fly; appearance + geometry/velocity block of equal size. Core change C-UMT (only if the precheck passes): fine-tune the FlyVis core on target identity ALONE (fly-only head, ranking loss over episode candidates), then freeze and fuse late with appearance; or train jointly with an auxiliary fly-only identity loss weighted so that the fly branch's gradient is not dominated (MMPareto-style), never with only the joint loss next to frozen MASA. Its equal control: a ~734-parameter unconstrained recurrent net on the same R1 crops trained with the same schedule. Condition to proceed to GPU: math_precheck (a) and (b) pass on fit104 nested folds and the OR-oracle gap is concentrated in motion-specific strata where R1 and geometry fail; and R-UME/R-RES on CPU show (A+F) - (A+R1) with a positive lower CI bound on fit104 before one-time confirmation on fresh videos (train26 has already been used once).
strongest_objection: The imbalance literature explains why a jointly TRAINED weak encoder is starved; in our experiments no encoder was trained - both MASA and FlyVis features were fixed and a gradient-boosting model, which keeps fitting residuals, combined them. Moreover the fly block was not ignored (AUC +0.008 over appearance), and the same gain arises from the raw eye input R1 (+0.006) and stock C (+0.007), with utility differences D-R1 -0.042 [-0.358; +0.280]. This pattern is what redundancy-with-the-input predicts, not imbalance: balancing remedies would amplify R1 as much as D and cannot produce a FlyVis-specific advantage. So the sources mainly supply a diagnostic and a stop rule, and a positive imbalance signature in Step 1 would yield at best a readout gain that must still beat R1 under the same scheme. Additionally, all supporting tables are on clip classification with modalities learned from scratch, with unstable re-run numbers and no equal-capacity null branch.
cost_and_hardware: math_precheck Steps 0-6: CPU only, saved arrays already on disk; per fold several LightGBM/XGBoost fits on ~40k (fit104) / 5345 labelled (train26) candidate rows plus bootstrap (5000 resamples over videos) - estimated 0.5-2 h CPU in total [uncertain: estimate, not measured]; the utility translation reuses the existing offline gate code. R-UME/R-RES readout variants: CPU, comparable cost. C-UMT core fine-tuning on identity: one 12 GB GPU; the earlier core continuation ran at 1.23-2.5 s/step (runs/z13_continue_20261017), so a 1000-4000-step unimodal pre-training per arm plus the equal-size unconstrained control is roughly 1-6 GPU hours per seed [uncertain], plus regeneration of FlyVis activity for all candidate crops; requires author permission under the project rules.
